CLINICAL DETAILS
Reason for referral: Family history of Lynch syndrome. Patient presents with colorectal adenomas at age 42. Sister diagnosed with endometrial cancer at age 38 and found to carry pathogenic MLH1 variant.

PATIENT HISTORY
Previous colonoscopy revealed multiple adenomatous polyps. No personal history of malignancy. BMI 28, non-smoker. Father died of colorectal cancer at age 55.

TEST PERFORMED
Targeted next-generation sequencing of Lynch syndrome genes (MLH1, MSH2, MSH6, PMS2, EPCAM) including full gene sequencing and deletion/duplication analysis. Library preparation using hybrid capture with Agilent SureSelect. Sequencing performed on Illumina NextSeq platform with minimum 100x coverage.

RESULTS

MLH1 (NM_000249.3): c.1852_1854delAAG p.(Lys618del)
Heterozygous deletion detected
Pathogenic variant (ClinVar ID: 90686)
Population frequency: 0.00001 (gnomAD v3.1)

MSH2 (NM_000251.2): No pathogenic variants detected
Mean coverage: 156x

MSH6 (NM_000179.2): No pathogenic variants detected  
Mean coverage: 142x

PMS2 (NM_000535.5): No pathogenic variants detected
Mean coverage: 98x (Note: Pseudogene regions excluded)

EPCAM (NM_002354.2): No deletions detected
MLPA analysis normal

MICROSATELLITE INSTABILITY TESTING
MSI analysis by PCR of tumor DNA (from archived polyp tissue):
BAT25: Stable
BAT26: Stable  
D2S123: Stable
D5S346: Stable
D17S250: Stable
Result: Microsatellite stable (MSS)

INTERPRETATION
The MLH1 c.1852_1854delAAG variant results in an in-frame deletion of lysine 618, located in the ATPase domain. This variant has been reported in multiple Lynch syndrome families and functional studies demonstrate impaired mismatch repair activity. The variant is classified as pathogenic according to ACMG/AMP criteria (PVS1, PS3, PM2, PP1).

The absence of microsatellite instability in the polyp tissue suggests this lesion may have developed through an alternative pathway, which can occur in Lynch syndrome-associated adenomas.

CLINICAL RECOMMENDATIONS
1. Enhanced colorectal surveillance with annual colonoscopy
2. Consider prophylactic hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy (discuss with gynecologic oncologist)
3. Annual endometrial sampling starting at age 30-35
4. Consider gastric and small bowel surveillance
5. Cascade testing recommended for at-risk relatives
6. Genetic counseling for family planning discussions

clinical_outcome.overall_implications: Patient carries pathogenic MLH1 variant confirming Lynch syndrome diagnosis. This confers high lifetime risk for colorectal cancer (up to 80%) and endometrial cancer (up to 60% in females)
